items.title: mattpocock/skills
items.summary: Mattpocock/skills brings together AI agent skills used in real engineering processes and supporting daily workflows. Designed to automate software development tasks, this toolkit offers a structure focused directly on practical applications.

snapshot.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory. My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding.

items.title: anthropics/skills
items.summary: The skills repository shared by Anthropic contains various application examples showcasing the capabilities of Claude models. Developed in the Python language, this project offers a wide range of AI workflows, from creative designs to technical web application tests.

snapshot.description: Public repository for Agent Skills. This repository contains skills that demonstrate what's possible with Claude's skills system. These skills range from creative applications (art, music, design) to technical tasks (testing web apps, MCP server generation) to enterprise workflows (communications, branding, etc.).

items.title: lightpanda-io/browser
items.summary: Lightpanda is a headless browser specifically developed for AI and automation processes. Written in the Zig language, this tool aims to optimize data collection operations by processing web pages rapidly over the network.

snapshot.description: Lightpanda: the headless browser designed for AI and automation. Requesting 933 real web pages over the network on a AWS EC2 m5.large instance. See benchmark details.

items.title: Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace
items.summary: A malicious backdoor was detected in the Claude Code for VS Code extension offered on the Cursor Marketplace. The security vulnerability in question posed a risk that could lead to unauthorized access to users' systems.

items.title: AI isn't replacing SREs, it's deskilling them
items.summary: The fact that AI takes over a large portion of incident response processes carries the risk of causing site reliability engineers (SREs) to lose their proficiency in critical situations. This raises the question of whether the convenience provided by automation might lead to the atrophy of engineering skills.

snapshot.description: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters?

items.title: Northflank Breached
items.summary: Cloud-based application development platform Northflank announced that it experienced a security breach in its systems. The company stated that investigations into the incident are ongoing and that it has taken the necessary measures to ensure the security of user data.

items.title: The $6.3B Binance hack was pulled off in just 20 minutes
items.summary: It is stated that the $6.3 billion cyberattack carried out on Binance was completed in just 20 minutes. The details of this incident targeting the cryptocurrency exchange Binance platform highlight the speed and scale of the attack.

items.title: Azure's Weakest Link – Five Full Cross-Tenant Compromises
items.summary: Architectural vulnerabilities in API connections (a digital bridge that allows two different software programs to communicate with each other), which are part of the Azure Logic Apps platform, lead to five different full cross-tenant breaches. These security vulnerabilities reveal risks regarding the security of structures that allow systems to access each other on the cloud computing service Azure.

snapshot.description: In my previous blog posts, Azure’s Weakest Link? and Azure’s Weakest Link - Full Cross-Tenant Compromise, I gave an overview of the severely insecure architecture behind API Connections in Azure, a part of Azure Logic Apps, and an instance of a full cross-tenant compromise using these inherent flaws.

items.title: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B
items.summary: NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B, developed by NVIDIA, is an open-weight automatic speech recognition model capable of transcribing in 40 languages. Supporting recordings of up to one hour, the model offers a 65,536-token context window with a hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture.

snapshot.description: automatic-speech-recognition model. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. Its hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture activates approximately 4.3B parameters, including the audio encoder, and it is released in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 precision.

items.title: baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2
items.summary: Unlimited-OCR-2, developed by Baidu, is an AI model that processes visual-based text to produce text output. The model has been tested on NVIDIA A800-80GB hardware to ensure compatibility with Python and various libraries.

snapshot.description: image-text-to-text model. Tested with Python 3.10, torch==2.13.0, transformers==4.52.1, huggingface-hub==0.36.0, tokenizers==0.21.4, on an NVIDIA A800-80GB:

items.title: EPSBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Earnings Forecasting
items.summary: EPSBench is an evaluation tool that measures the ability of large language models (LLMs) to make quarterly earnings forecasts for companies based on financial reports, earnings call transcripts, and news. Using 149 quarters of data from 86 US companies, this system tests the ability of AI agents to correlate financial evidence with income statement items.

snapshot.description: Quarterly earnings forecasting requires an agent to connect financial evidence to the income-statement line items that produce a company's reported earnings. We introduce EPSBench, a benchmark for studying this ability across 149 firm-quarters from 86 US companies. Agents read a fixed collection of filings, earnings-call transcripts, and news, then estimate company-specific income-statement drivers with cited evidence. items.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face introduces the weakening-induced on-policy self-distillation method developed for training large reasoning models. This approach, called WISD, creates a training signal by comparing the model with its own weakened version when an external teacher model is not available.

snapshot.description: Self-distillation offers a way to improve reasoning models when a suitable external teacher is unavailable. However, common approaches rely on privileged information to construct a stronger self-teacher, limiting their use when only unlabeled prompts are available. In this paper, we introduce Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation (WISD), which instead constructs a weaker counterpart of the original model and uses the contrast between the two as a training signal without requiring privile

items.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face aims to enable generation in any order in pre-trained autoregressive image models without being bound to a fixed scanning order. This method allows models to perform image inpainting, outpainting, and editing operations without additional training costs.

snapshot.description: Autoregressive (AR) image generators are powerful in principle but inflexible in practice: training with a fixed raster-scan order hardcodes a single factorization of the image distribution into the model, leaving it unable to inpaint, outpaint, or edit at inference time. items.title: Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents
items.summary: The study titled 'Matched Capabilities, Different Behaviors: A Controlled Study of MCP and CLI Interfaces for Language Agents' examines the tool usage of language agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and command-line interfaces (CLI). The research analyzes how different interface representations change the decision-making processes and behaviors of AI agents, even when the same functional capabilities are provided.

snapshot.description: Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. Model Context Protocol (MCP) and command-line interfaces (CLI) can expose the same semantic operations through markedly different model-facing representations. items.title: Broken on Arrival: Non-Functional Quantized LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face addresses the functionality issues of quantized large language models (LLMs) found in public repositories. The research shows that some of the tested models fail in coding tasks and that there is a lack of a standard testing process for verifying these files.

snapshot.description: Developers download quantized large language models (LLMs) from public registries to run them locally. None of the registries we examined documented functional testing of their files. We tested all 305 eligible code-capable GGUF tags (the llama.cpp format) across 15 model lines in the official Ollama library, plus 22 popular Hugging Face community files.
